breaking.headline: Nvidia beats big and guides to $130 billion; shares jump after hours
breaking.fact: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago and about $6.7 billion above consensus, with adjusted EPS of $2.68 against $2.47 expected and data-center revenue of $107.6 billion. It guided Q4 revenue to $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above the roughly $125 billion analysts expected, assuming no data-center chip sales to China. Shares rose about 3% after hours in the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress, ahead of the 5 p.m. ET call.

breaking.headline: NSA says outage was routine-maintenance glitch, not a cyberattack
breaking.fact: The NSA said Tuesday its classified internal network, NSA Net, suffered “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, with mission-critical capabilities fully operational. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the outage stemmed from patching PHP software vulnerabilities discovered last month, and there is no sign any of the recent tech outages, including the NSA’s, was a cyberattack. Restoration was still under way Tuesday afternoon.

breaking.headline: Disney beats Q4 estimates, hikes dividend 33%, plans $3 billion in savings
breaking.fact: Disney reported fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.77, up 59% from a year ago and above the $1.68 analysts expected, on revenue of $25.95 billion, up 16%. Streaming operating income doubled to $824 million and parks revenue rose 15% to $10.1 billion. The company raised its annual dividend 33% to $2.00 a share and outlined $3 billion in run-rate savings by fiscal 2029.

breaking.headline: Anthropic order book closes; IPO to price Wednesday, trade Thursday
breaking.fact: Anthropic’s order book closed at 4 p.m. ET Tuesday; CNBC’s David Faber, citing sources, says the IPO is likely to price above the $70–$78 range. The final price is set Wednesday and trading begins Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner put in a $5 billion order, and demand is running about seven times the 825 million shares on offer.

weekInBrief.headline: Retail sales rise 0.2% in October; Home Depot beats and lifts outlook
weekInBrief.body: U.S. retail sales rose 0.2% in October, matching expectations, in a sign the consumer is holding up. Home Depot reported third-quarter sales of $43.4 billion, up 4.9%, with comparable sales up 2.2% and adjusted EPS of $3.86, and raised its full-year sales growth outlook to 4.5%.

weekInBrief.headline: Extended half-life RSV antibody shows broad activity, high barrier to resistance
weekInBrief.body: An extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody, RSM01, showed broad neutralizing activity against circulating RSV strains with a high barrier to resistance in lab tests, researchers report in Nature Communications. The findings support RSM01 as an alternative should resistance emerge to current licensed anti-RSV antibodies.

weekInBrief.headline: China’s thermal power falls for a fourth straight month as wind and solar grow
weekInBrief.body: China’s thermal power generation fell year on year for a fourth straight month in October as wind and solar generation grew, extending the shift in the world’s largest power system away from coal-fired output.

weekInBrief.headline: Wind farms and clouds shape each other, Dutch study finds
weekInBrief.body: Researchers in the Netherlands found that offshore wind farms and clouds influence each other, with the interaction depending on weather conditions, particularly cloud height — a finding that matters for forecasting power output as wind farms scale up. The work was presented by the American Institute of Physics.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iranian state media claimed Tuesday that four tankers struck naval mines in the strait over the past two days — none of those claims has been independently verified. Iran’s foreign minister held closed-door talks in Islamabad on Tuesday with Pakistan’s army chief as Tehran presses its conditions for reopening the strait. On oil, the blockade still holds — UANI’s Nov. 16 update says no Iranian crude tanker has evaded it since July 14, while CENTCOM said Nov. 14 that Gulf partners have moved more than 1.7 billion barrels of non-Iranian crude through the strait under U.S. protection.

space.headline: Perseverance finds water-linked rocks beyond Jezero crater
space.body: NASA’s Perseverance rover found a cluster of unusually bright rocks rich in hydrated silica in an area called Idubi, outside Jezero crater. The mineral forms in watery environments and can preserve microscopic fossils on Earth, making the rocks a prime target for studying Mars’s water history and past habitability. A close-up science campaign is already under way.

space.headline: Webb: galaxy outflows quench star formation at ‘cosmic noon’
space.body: James Webb Space Telescope observations show massive galaxies drive large-scale gaseous outflows that shut down their star production, researchers report. The study links outflows from a massive galaxy’s central core to the quenching of star formation at so-called cosmic noon, roughly 8–12 billion years ago, when star formation across the universe peaked.

space.headline: Diamond maser amplifies quantum signals 1,000-fold
space.body: Researchers at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology built a diamond-based microwave amplifier — a maser — that operates near absolute zero and boosts weak signals more than 1,000-fold while adding noise close to the minimum quantum mechanics allows. The device, described in Nature Communications, is a tool for quantum-computer readout, sensing and dark-matter searches.

space.headline: Melanoma protein patterns predict immunotherapy response
space.body: Researchers at Mount Sinai and the National Cancer Institute identified three protein patterns in skin melanoma linked to treatment response after combination immunotherapy. The immune-rich pattern had the most favorable progression-free survival, and the team built a classifier to assign tumors to the groups. The companion studies appear in Clinical Cancer Research and Cancer Discovery.

apod.title: Major Fireball Meteor
apod.credit: Ollie Taylor — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 8, 2026
apod.explanation: A bright fireball meteor flashes east to west under the Big Dipper over the Dolomite Alps above La Villa, Italy, captured by chance during a camera exposure on a subfreezing November night in 2017. Sightings were widely reported across European skies, making it one of the most reported fireball events ever; its track over Germany matches the Northern Taurid meteor shower, dust from Comet Encke.
